paragraphs: In the morning, a technician receives a boat that will not start, checks the fuel and ignition systems, and identifies the failed part. They disassemble and clean components and replace gaskets. In the afternoon, they check the electronic controls and propeller and adjust idle speed. After a water test confirms there are no unusual noises, they complete the work order and estimate and return the boat to its owner.

In one sentence: repair and tune marine engines so they run properly. The work includes inspecting engines and drive systems, performing maintenance and replacing parts, troubleshooting faults, adjusting fuel systems and electronic controls, conducting water tests and final inspections, and recording labor and estimates.
